read.title: Energy changes form
text: In physics, work has a narrow meaning: a force does work when it moves something along the force's direction. Carrying a bag across a level room at steady speed does no work on the bag by the upward force of your arm, because that force is perpendicular to the motion. Lifting the bag does work, storing gravitational potential energy mgh.

The work–energy theorem ties work to motion. The net work done on an object equals its change in kinetic energy, ½mv². Because speed is squared, doubling a car's speed quadruples its kinetic energy and roughly quadruples its braking distance.

Gravity and ideal springs are conservative forces: the work they do depends only on the start and end points, so they have potential energies. When only conservative forces do work, kinetic plus potential energy stays constant. A skier sliding down a frictionless hill reaches the same bottom speed whether the slope is gentle or steep, because only the height lost matters.

Friction is nonconservative. It still conserves total energy, but it converts mechanical energy into thermal energy that cannot easily be recovered. Power measures how fast energy is transferred; one watt is one joule per second.
